note: Joining two positions with one word for the way across, "the crossing": position 2 alone, then the crossing on a position-neck with cross, then phrases that use it over drums and bass. Two positions are on the screen, so each is numbered with its scale the first time. Key and tempo are moves (any key, 70 to 90 bpm), which carry what guitar-intermediate-joining-boxes did with a second key in C; its crossing on a string the learner picks is now the last line of the crossing section, named by the "Cross on" buttons under the neck.

exercise.title: {{=key}} minor pentatonic: join positions 1 and 2
exercise.why: Position 2 starts on the notes where position 1 ends, so one slide along one string carries a phrase from the first into the second.

cells.text:
Press the first Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Under it is the neck with position 2 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale: each dot is a note to play, and the ringed dots are the {{1}} notes.
Start on the lowest dot on the low E string and play both dots on each string up to the high e string, then come back down the same way, one note per beat.
The goal of this practice is to find the ringed {{1}} notes without looking at the neck.

The neck below shows only the crossing: position 1 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale on the low strings, position 2 on the high strings. Start on {{1}} on the low E string and climb position 1. On the G string, slide from the ringed {{4}} up to the ringed {{5}} and finish the climb in position 2.
Come back down the same way, sliding from {{5}} down to {{4}}.
Once the slide lands without looking, press another string beside Cross on under the neck and make the crossing there: same move, new drill.

Press the first Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass in {{=key}}. Make up short phrases that start in position 1 and use the crossing to end in position 2, then phrases that go back the other way. End each phrase on one of the ringed {{1}} notes.
{{?key}}In another key both positions sit on other frets, and the crossing is still the slide from {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string.
